summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase loop for GSD Phase 66 (api-schema-cutover-publish-gate-and-tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews.
summary.outcome: Steps 1–6 completed: verification confirmed passing, security audit found and fixed a real write-privilege escalation (T-66-E1), SDK E2E gate green, simplify removed dead code and stale comment, CodeRabbit CLI triaged 15 findings (2 fixed in-scope, 3 deferred as todos, 9 false positives/already-handled), 66-SECURITY.md written as SECURED. Two commits landed; Steps 7–10 (ship, PR reviews, CI confirmation) not yet reached.

repo: 89 SDK E2E tests across 11 suites are pre-existing `D-01` milestone quarantines (`describe.skip` with comment 're-enable at phase 63-65'), not Phase 66 regressions — safe to ignore in this gate.
Phase 66 deleted all 5 shares spec files (including share-invite.service.spec.ts) without rewriting them for the new descriptor-ref model, leaving reshared shares logic with zero unit coverage.
The pre-commit api-client hook only blocks when openapi.json has real semantic changes; `@Matches` DTO validators do NOT surface regex patterns into the OpenAPI spec.
`pnpm api:generate` runs repo-wide `eslint .` at the end and fails on a pre-existing triple-slash-reference error in `landing/.astro/types.d.ts` (generated Astro file) — unrelated to code changes.
All IPNS controller endpoints (publish/batch/unenroll/resolve) carry `@Throttle` decorators; the phase-new `tombstone` endpoint was missing one.
Sibling IPNS DTOs (`resolve`, `tombstone`) use a strict `k51qzi5uqu5…|bafzaa…` regex; `create-share.dto` and `create-invite.dto` used the loose `/^k[a-z0-9]+$/` — inconsistency left by this phase.

GSD security enforcement step hook was toggled off in config (`workflow.security_block_on` present but no active `verify:post` hook), requiring the secure-phase workflow to be run explicitly rather than auto-gated.
The `ApiSchemaCutover` migration was already applied to `cipherbox_test` (no pending migrations) — suite only needs `migration:run` as a precondition check, not a fresh apply.

code.finding: T-66-E1 write-privilege escalation: claim path stored `dto.writeDescriptorRef` (claimer-supplied) on the minted Share without gating on `invite.writeDescriptorRef` (sharer's granted authority), allowing a read-only invite to yield a write grant. Comment at 178 claimed the gate existed but the code didn't implement it.

Private `upsertIpnsRecord` method had an unused `_publicKey?` parameter (underscore-flagged); single call site passed `undefined`. Safe to remove — all 174 IPNS unit tests confirmed behavior-neutral after removal.
`hasSigData` guard (`result.pubKey && …`) already fails-closed on pubKey recovery failure — CodeRabbit finding #14 about partial sig bundles was a false positive.
Used loose `/^k[a-z0-9]+$/` for `rootIpnsName` instead of the canonical strict pattern used by all sibling IPNS DTOs.
Same loose IPNS regex as create-share.dto — both tightened to canonical pattern in this session.
psql helper calls in both assertion helpers had no statement timeouts, making the suite susceptible to hanging on DB stalls (CodeRabbit F4; timeouts added).

workflow: The GSD security auditor and CodeRabbit CLI independently corroborated the same vulnerability (T-66-E1 write-descriptor gating) — running both provides adversarial cross-validation.

After `pnpm api:generate`, diff the output with `git diff --stat` and do a canonicalized semantic comparison (`jq -S . | diff`) before staging — formatting-only churn (trailing commas, line wraps) should be reverted to avoid noisy commits.
CodeRabbit CLI streams findings incrementally; the count grew from 3 → 9 → 15 across polling intervals. Always wait for exit 0 and extract the full deduplicated set before triaging.

A clean API boot (health check passes = DI resolves) conclusively disproves 'entity still injected' false positives without needing further grep — proved FolderIpns removal was complete despite 4 CodeRabbit 'criticals'.

Prettier/eslint reformatting via `api:generate` can silently touch unrelated files (migration timestamps, migration class formatting) — always inspect `git diff --stat` after generation and revert anything outside intended scope before committing.
Build → restart API → re-run E2E cycle after each batch of edits is necessary; skipping the restart means testing against a stale dist that doesn't reflect the latest changes.

friction: CodeRabbit CLI failed on first attempt with a service connection error, requiring a retry.

`pnpm api:generate` fails at the final `eslint .` step on a pre-existing error in `landing/.astro/types.d.ts` (generated Astro file) — prevents clean generation runs and produces misleading exit codes.

`pnpm api:generate` reformatted `openapi.json` (cosmetic array wrapping) and `ApiSchemaCutover.ts` migration (trailing commas) with zero semantic change, requiring explicit `git restore` to avoid committing noise.
GSD's `api:generate` eslint-failure path doesn't distinguish pre-existing errors from new ones — looks like a real failure even when caused by an unrelated gitignored generated file.
